We just won $15k at the Consensus 2026 hackathon! We built Parabola (on Solana ) - an estimation market where you bet a full distribution of outcomes, instead of a few discrete options (e.g. how many people show up to Consensus 2026, not just over/under 20K) Massive thanks to my teammates Aadit Jerfy , Prashanth Bhaskara , shikhar sehgal, and to Phil Kwok and Dom K. at EasyA for the advice and mentorship. Missed 3 days of school, a concerning amount of sleep, and almost my flight back - was definitely worth it though. Can’t wait to continue building this and see where it goes. Read more here: https://lnkd.in/gczccxR6 ...more

I’ve written over 100 LinkedIn posts. Only 5 went viral. 90 were mediocre. 5 were absolutely atrocious. Every post is a risk. Anyone could see it: • Your friends • Your teachers • Your colleagues But people have short memories. Nobody remembers what you posted 6-7 posts ago. So if it flops, nobody notices. If it pops off, everyone sees. Waiting for your first viral post is the hardest part. But once you’ve done it once, you know you can do it again.

IBM Quantum is coming to UChicago this fall! I'm excited to have been selected as the lead organizer for the annual IBM Qiskit Fall Fest 2026 at the University of Chicago , in partnership with the IBM Quantum Computing team! This is an exciting moment for our community: UChicago will now become an official IBM Quantum Network institution, and I can't wait to help bring that partnership to life by working together with Sanda Bostan ! Fall Fest is a global initiative that brings students together to learn, build, and explore the future of quantum computing — and I'm glad I get to help create that experience for my fellow students at UChicago! More details on speakers, workshops, and registration coming soon! If you're interested in quantum computing or want to get involved, reach out!

I’m flying home after 2 weeks in the US. (And I’ll remember this trip for the rest of my life) On the flight from NYC, I sat next to a stranger. We talked the whole way and ended up hanging out for the next 3 days. In SF, I had the best tacos of my life at 11pm in Tenderloin (a sketchy area). It was so good we went back twice. In LA, I drove a Ferrari for the first time. Being only 19, I was surprised they even let me sit in the car. There was an instructor next to me and I was still terrified I’d scratch it. But the best part was the people. Old friends. New friends. People I’d only known online. You learn more in an hour with someone who’s done it before than a month of reading. So travel young. And talk to strangers. Thank you to everyone who gave me their time. And I’m glad I got to share these experiences with my good friend James Wingfield .

When I arrived in SF two years ago, I camped out at SPC figuring out to do next. They provide a two story building for builders to just hang out and dream big in for six months. Some people start companies and other decide to join one. I explored both but chose the latter, and I’m so grateful I had the time, space and community to get it right. Congrats to them on this huge raise to keep helping builders find their next thing.
